He deposed that he was the president of the said society while co-accused was the secretary and father of co- accused was executive director of the said society.

15. This being a criminal case, the burden of proving guilt of accused lies upon the prosecution for which the standard required is beyond reasonable doubt.

The main ingredient of the offences State vs Vijay Narain on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180052743/
3 alleged in the present case is collection of funds from members of Raj Laxmi Housing Society and subsequent transfer of approximately Rs. 1.24 Crore by accused persons to Shri Ram Housing Company and thereby, misappropriation of funds by accused persons.

State Vs.Vijay Narain & Anr.
FIR No.: 374/1994 P.S.:Lajpat Nagar 16.

As already noted above, none of the public witnesses, who were stated by the prosecution to be members of Raj Laxmi Housing Society and investors in the said society, have made any incriminating statement against the accused persons.

All the said public witnesses have categorically stated that they have received their money back through the court appointed Administrator and they do not have any further grievance against the accused persons.

Thus, the public witnesses who are allegedly victims in the present matter, have all failed to depose the relevant facts to establish commission of alleged offences by the accused persons in the present matter and the same is fatal to the case of the prosecution.

17. For the alleged offence of cheating, it was necessary for the prosecution to establish dishonest inducement by accused persons to victims to make payment and thereafter, to establish wrongful loss caused by such payment to the said victims.
In the instant case, the victims had invested money/deposited funds with the Raj Laxmi Housing Society for the purpose of allotment of land by DDA.
However, the said allotment of land was to be made on payment of installments by the said housing society to DDA, which was not made in the present matter.
Thus, the prosecution has actually failed to establish that the accused persons had intention to not make payment to DDA at the time of inducing the members of society to make payment.

Such dishonest intention since beginning is negated by the fact that initially, some payment was made to DDA and same is also State Vs.Vijay Narain & Anr.
FIR No.: 374/1994 P.S.:Lajpat Nagar admitted by the prosecution in this case.
18.

Furthermore, the justification given by accused persons for not being able to make further payment of installments to DDA is that many members of the said housing society defaulted in making further deposits and therefore, the payment of installments to DDA could not be made in timely manner.

This defence of accused persons has been supported by PW7, who has admitted in his examination in chief dated 16.05.2013 that "thereafter from time to time, I was asked to pay installments in that housing society but I did not pay".

Furthermore, none of the public witnesses have categorically deposed that failure to pay installments to DDA by the said housing society was because the accused persons had misappropriated the funds of the said housing society already deposited by the investors/members of the said housing society.
The crucial chain linking non-payment to DDA with alleged misappropriation by accused persons is missing from the evidence of all public witnesses.
19. Furthermore, investigation with respect to alleged misappropriation of funds is shoddy at best.

It is the case of prosecution that accused Vijay Narain and his father were office bearers of Shri Ram State vs Vijay Narain on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180052743/

sentences.text: Housing Finance Company, to whom funds had been transferred from Raj Laxmi Group Housing Society.
Thus, the beneficiaries of the alleged misappropriation was not only the present accused persons, but also father of accused Vijay State Vs.Vijay Narain & Anr.
FIR No.: 374/1994 P.S.:Lajpat Nagar Narain.
There is no explanation given by prosecution as to why he was not made an accused in the present matter.
Furthermore, the investigation has not given any details of the manner in which the allegedly misappropriated money was used for personal gain by accused persons.
It is vaguely stated in the final report that the allegedly misappropriated money was used for personal benefit like purchasing of house, car etc.
Thus, crucial evidence to establish misappropriation for personal gain, beyond reasonable doubt, by the prosecution is also missing in the present trial.
For the purpose of misappropriation, only the disclosure statements of accused persons have been relied upon in the present charge sheet, which is inadmissible as per Section 25 Indian Evidence Act.
20. Accused persons have also claimed that transfer of money was made to Sri Ram Housing Finance after resolution was passed to this effect in meeting dated 31.03.1991 of the said society.
However, no such document has been produced during trial.
In order dated 16.08.2005, it was noted that Ld. APP had made submissions regarding the said resolution being fake.

However, in the same order, the Ld. Predecessor also placed reliance upon judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Orissa vs. Devendra Nath Padhi , 2005(1) JCC 109 and did not consider the resolution dated 31.03.1991 for the purpose of framing charge upon accused persons.

entities.text: State of Orissa vs. Devendra Nath Padhi , 2005(1) JCC 109
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the said document was a document of accused, used during arguments on charge and it was upon the accused to produce the same during State Vs.Vijay Narain & Anr.
FIR No.: 374/1994 P.S.:Lajpat Nagar defence.
However, no such document has been produced, but oral evidence of DW2 has been given that such meeting dated 31.03.1991 had indeed taken place.

Without document, the oral evidence cannot be relied upon as no permission to lead secondary evidence has also been taken by accused persons during trial. Be that as it may, the same is not fatal to the defence of accused persons, as in view of above discussion, the prosecution has not been able to discharge its burden of proof.

21. During testimony of PW12, it has come on record that documents which were seized vide seizure memo Ex.PW12/B, during investigation had been filed with the present charge-sheet but could not be traced on record.
A separate fact finding inquiry is on-going in the present matter.

However,
perusal of the said seizure memo clearly shows that all documents maintained by the concerned Society with respect to contributions received, cash memos and receipt books, etc. were seized, but the same are not relevant for the purpose of establishing guilt of accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
The records of the said society is anyhow not disputed by accused persons during trial, and it is not the case of prosecution that accused persons would not be acquitted, if not for those records.

22. Thus, as a cumulative effect of all the points discussed above, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and benefit of State Vs.Vijay Narain & Anr.
